code: site/ ├── app.R ├── api.R ├── pages/      # one template per page │   ├── index.html │   ├── cars.html │   └── model.html ├── partials/   # shared by every page │   ├── head.html │   ├── nav.html │   └── footer.html └── www/     ├── site.css     ├── cars.js     └── model.js # spigot "site" example: a small multi-page site about R's mtcars data. # # * Three pages, each a whisker template in pages/, sharing the partials in #   partials/ (the <head>, the nav bar and the footer). # * The /cars page is rendered in R with every row; its filter form then #   calls the API and redraws the table in the browser. # * The /model page calls an endpoint that bootstraps a regression in a #   future worker, another R process, so the app keeps serving other tabs. # # Run it with spigot::run_example("site"). It needs the future package. library(spigot)  # The fit endpoint hands its work to background R processes. future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 2) shiny::onStop(function() future::plan(future::sequential))  cars <- data.frame(model = rownames(datasets::mtcars), datasets::mtcars, row.names = NULL) predictors <- c(   wt = "Weight (1000 lbs)", hp = "Horsepower", disp = "Displacement (cu. in.)",   qsec = "Quarter-mile time (s)", drat = "Rear axle ratio" )  # A page of the site: its template, the shared partials, and its data. `key` # tells the nav partial which link is the current page. The data never # changes, so each page is rendered once and cached. page <- function(file, key, title, data = list()) {   spigot_page(     file.path("pages", file),     data = c(list(title = title, page = stats::setNames(list(TRUE), key)), data),     partials = list(       head = "partials/head.html",       nav = "partials/nav.html",       footer = "partials/footer.html"     ),     cache = TRUE   ) }  spigot_app(   pages = list(     "/" = page("index.html", "home", "Home", list(       n = nrow(cars),       predictors = length(predictors)     )),     "/cars" = page("cars.html", "cars", "Cars", list(       rows = unname(whisker::rowSplit(cars[c("model", "mpg", "cyl", "hp", "wt")]))     )),     "/model" = page("model.html", "model", "Model", list(       predictors = Map(function(name, label) list(name = name, label = label),                        names(predictors), unname(predictors), USE.NAMES = FALSE)     ))   ),   api = "api.R" )

code: # The site's API. `cars` and `predictors` are defined in app.R: spigot_app() # evaluates this file in app.R's environment.  #* Cars whose model name contains `q` (ignoring case) and that do at least #* `min_mpg` miles per gallon. #* @get /cars function(q = "", min_mpg = "") {   min_mpg <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(min_mpg))   if (length(min_mpg) != 1 || is.na(min_mpg)) min_mpg <- -Inf   keep <- grepl(tolower(q), tolower(cars$model), fixed = TRUE) & cars$mpg >= min_mpg   # A data frame becomes an array of row objects.   list(rows = cars[keep, c("model", "mpg", "cyl", "hp", "wt")]) }  #* Regress mpg on one predictor and bootstrap a 95% interval for the slope. #* The work runs in a future worker, another R process, so this R process #* keeps serving other requests while it runs. #* @post /fit function(res, x = "wt", reps = 1000) {   if (!is.character(x) || length(x) != 1 || !x %in% names(predictors)) {     res$status <- 400L     return(list(error = paste("x must be one of:", paste(names(predictors), collapse = ", "))))   }   reps <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(reps))   if (length(reps) != 1 || is.na(reps) || reps < 100 || reps > 5000) {     res$status <- 400L     return(list(error = "reps must be a whole number from 100 to 5000"))   }    # Only these values are sent to the worker.   data <- cars[c("mpg", x)]   app_pid <- Sys.getpid()   promises::future_promise({     started <- Sys.time()     slope <- function(d) unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(d$mpg ~ d[[x]]))[2])     boots <- replicate(reps, slope(data[sample.int(nrow(data), replace = TRUE), ]))     ci <- unname(stats::quantile(boots, c(0.025, 0.975)))     list(       x = x,       reps = reps,       slope = list(estimate = slope(data), lower = ci[1], upper = ci[2]),       seconds = as.numeric(Sys.time() - started, units = "secs"),       worker_pid = Sys.getpid(),       app_pid = app_pid     )   }, seed = TRUE)   # The endpoint returns the promise; spigot sends the reply when it resolves. }

text: app.R keeps shared state environment endpoints server function see, broadcasts number open tabs one opens closes: increment endpoint uses three channels: reply carries new count, broadcast tells every tab, trigger tells calling tab’s server function. page’s script listens events, loads current state , calls API buttons:
code: # spigot "live" example: a counter shared by every open tab. It uses all three # channels between a page and R: # # * HTTP: the page reads and changes the count with spigot.get() and #   spigot.post() (api.R). # * Push: R sends every open tab the new count with spigot_broadcast(), and #   the page listens with spigot.on(). # * Bridge: the endpoint also sets an input of the calling tab with #   spigot_trigger(), so that tab's server function updates a Shiny output #   on the page. # # Run it with spigot::run_example("live"), then open the page in a second tab. library(shiny) library(spigot)  # State shared by every tab. It lives in this R process, so the endpoints in # api.R (evaluated in this environment) and the server function see the same # values. shared <- new.env() shared$count <- 0L shared$tabs <- 0L  server <- function(input, output, session) {   # A tab opened or closed: tell every tab how many are open.   shared$tabs <- shared$tabs + 1L   spigot_broadcast("tabs", list(tabs = shared$tabs))   session$onSessionEnded(function() {     shared$tabs <- shared$tabs - 1L     spigot_broadcast("tabs", list(tabs = shared$tabs))   })    # This tab's own clicks. The increment endpoint sets input$clicked with   # spigot_trigger(); the page shows output$mine in an element with the   # class "shiny-text-output".   mine <- reactiveVal(0L)   observeEvent(input$clicked, mine(mine() + input$clicked))   output$mine <- renderText(mine()) }  spigot_app(   pages = spigot_page("index.html"),   server = server,   api = "api.R" ) # The example's API. `shared` is defined in app.R: spigot_app() evaluates this # file in app.R's environment.  #* The count and the number of open tabs. A plain HTTP read. #* @get /state function() {   list(count = shared$count, tabs = shared$tabs) }  #* Add `by` (1 to 10) to the count, tell every tab, and tell this tab's #* server function. #* @post /increment function(req, res, by = 1) {   by <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(by))   if (length(by) != 1 || is.na(by) || by < 1 || by > 10) {     res$status <- 400L     return(list(error = "by must be a whole number from 1 to 10"))   }   shared$count <- shared$count + by    # Push: every open tab, this one included, gets the new count.   spigot_broadcast("count", list(count = shared$count, by = by))   # Bridge: this tab's server function sees input$clicked change.   spigot_trigger(spigot_session(req), "clicked", by)    list(count = shared$count) } // The page's only script. spigot_app() adds spigot.js, which defines spigot.get(), // spigot.post() and spigot.on().  const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);  // The count only goes up, so show the highest value seen. A reply and a push // can arrive in either order: R sends the push while the endpoint runs, so it // can reach the page before the reply to the same request. let shown = -1; function showCount(n) {   if (n <= shown) return;   shown = n;   $("count").textContent = n; }  const lines = []; function log(line) {   lines.push(`${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}  ${line}`);   $("log").textContent = lines.slice(-10).join("\n"); }  // Push: R calls spigot_broadcast() when the count changes or a tab opens or closes. spigot.on("count", (msg) => {   showCount(msg.count);   log(`push  count: ${msg.count} (+${msg.by})`); }); spigot.on("tabs", (msg) => {   $("tabs").textContent = msg.tabs;   log(`push  tabs: ${msg.tabs}`); });  // HTTP: read the current state once. spigot.get() waits for the Shiny session. spigot.get("state").then((s) => {   showCount(s.count);   $("tabs").textContent = s.tabs; });  async function add(by) {   try {     const reply = await spigot.post("increment", { by });     showCount(reply.count);     log(`reply count: ${reply.count}`);   } catch (err) {     if (!(err instanceof spigot.SpigotError)) throw err;     log(`reply ${err.status}: ${err.message}`);   } }  $("plus-one").addEventListener("click", () => add(1)); $("plus-five").addEventListener("click", () => add(5)); $("plus-bad").addEventListener("click", () => add(11));

text: First release. spigot_app() mounts plumber router inside Shiny app, hand-written pages (spigot_page()) call R endpoints origin port spigot.js.
